why: It reproduces the recurrence and maximum rule and identifies exactly which paper hypotheses are unnecessary.
text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer and $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. Assume $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$ for $j\ge1$. The formal statement proves $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for every $j\ge1$. The last formula is exactly (1.15), since $L_i=4\log\lambda_{i+1}$. The maximum is the greatest admissible integer. In the paper, $\mathcal B$ is also nondecreasing and dominates the fixed-order analytic constants, and $b$ is fixed by the later construction. These extra restrictions are unnecessary for the arithmetic conclusion. The formal statement is therefore stronger: it proves the same assertions under fewer hypotheses. Frequencies are real, while derivative orders and the exponents $K(s)$ are nonnegative integers; the hypotheses force the relevant frequencies to be positive.

why: Removes a false parameter-uniform inference while giving the exact valid cosine consequence and the missing smallness hypothesis.
text: For $\varepsilon>0$ and $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$, put $\varphi(\tau)=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal statement proves $2/\varepsilon\le\tan\varphi(\tau_m)\le9/(2\varepsilon)$. It assumes only the displayed time bracket; it does not assert that $\tau_m$ is a zero of a reference slope or a maximum of an amplitude. The resulting cosine bounds are $\varepsilon/\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+81/4}\le\cos\varphi(\tau_m)\le\varepsilon/\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+4}$. Concluding that this cosine is comparable to $\varepsilon$ requires an upper bound on $\varepsilon$, such as $\varepsilon\le1$, which the paper’s application supplies but this statement does not assume. No differential equation or amplitude estimate is used in this scalar calculation.

why: Makes the distinction between supplied label force and an actual Eulerian pullback explicit, without attributing a flow to arbitrary coefficient data.
text: On $[0,T]$, let $F,M$ be smooth unit-periodic matrix fields, and let $G$ satisfy $GF=FG=I$. Assume $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Put $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. For a supplied label force $f_{\rm lab}$, a smooth mean solution consists of smooth unit-periodic fields $v,z,B,\mathsf q$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $B=Fv$ and $B_t+MB+G^T\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\rm lab}$ on the closed interval. These are defining conditions, not an existence assertion. No spatial mean normalization of $\mathsf q$ is imposed. An actual flow is not part of these data. Only after separately identifying $F=D_aX$, $M=DU\circ X$ and $f_{\rm lab}=f\circ X$ may one interpret $Fz$ as particle displacement and $B\circ X^{-1}$ as the Eulerian correction.

why: It states the exact hypotheses, spaces, coefficient bounds, source factor and order of constants, and identifies the improvement over the paper.
text: Let $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$ and $L_0\ge0$. On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, take smooth matrix fields $F,M$ satisfying $F_t=MF$, with $F^{-1}$ defined, $\|F^{-1}\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L_0$ and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as a quadratic form. Put $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Suppose the nonnegative constants $K_0,K_1,\Omega_0,\Omega_1$ bound $\|K\|,\|D_aK\|,\|\Omega\|,\|D_a\Omega\|$ uniformly in the Euclidean operator norms. There is a universal $C\ge0$, chosen before all these data, with $A=C(D+L_0+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^{1164}$. For every $L\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3))$, the formal statement supplies unique divergence-free $v\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2})$ and $c\in C^{0,1/2}$ satisfying $Kv-\int_0^t\Omega v+L=c+\nabla_a\phi$, where $c$ is independent of time, $z(t)=\int_0^tv$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, and $\phi$ has zero mean with $\nabla_a\phi\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2})$. It gives $\|v\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le A\|L\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$ and $\|(\mathbb P K(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|\le A$, where $\mathbb P$ is the Leray projection and the inverse acts on divergence-free fields. The spatial Hölder norm is the maximum of supremum and seminorm. The polynomial uses supremum bounds for the coefficients and their first derivatives; the paper uses their larger $C^{1,1/2}$ norms. The abstract fields $F,M$ need not have been obtained from a specified flow.

why: It states both norm estimates and explains the global-profile input, cell continuation, ordered derivative multiplicities, and opposite changes of scope.
text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. The parent $U$ is a smooth odd divergence-free field on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$ and flow $X$. The bounds $\|\nabla U\|_\infty,\|D_aX\|_\infty,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$ hold. For a smooth periodic pressure $p_U$, set $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$; require $R_U$ odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-\nabla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The formal statement imposes these conditions directly. The paper selects the zero-mean Poisson pressure; the formal statement permits any pressure meeting the displayed conditions, without separately requiring $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$.

Write $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla U)\circ X$ and $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$, where $k_*\ne0$. Choose $0\le t_0<T$ with $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$. At the origin take a nonzero transverse solution $\mathbf a$ of $\mathbf a_t=-M\mathbf a+2\kappa(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$. Put $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. For every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, assume $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$, and assume $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ at the origin. The formal normalization is $0<\gamma\le1$; the paper additionally requires $\max\gamma=1$. Fix $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ for a sufficiently large integer $a$, and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$.

For a profile $f(t,a,s)$, the norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ sums $\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j f|$ over $|\alpha|+j\le n$ on $[0,T]$. The weighted norm $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ uses $[t_0,T]$ and divides by $\gamma(t)$; it differentiates only labels and phase. Each multi-index is counted once. The profiles are smooth on the closed time slab, one-periodic in $s$, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. Their stipulated zero values outside the time slab do not assert smoothness across its endpoints.

Let $g_0$ be such a profile with values in a real normed space, independent of phase outside the repeated support of the envelope. Here $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$ uses the fixed smooth radial cutoff, equal to one for $|a|\le\ell_*$ and zero for $|a|\ge2\ell_*$, with its support repeated over the label lattice. Define its physical field by $g_0^\natural(t,x)=g_0(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ with $a=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(x)$. The transformation rule of the profile ensures periodicity in $x$ even when $k_*\notin\mathbb Z^3$. For $t\in[t_0,T]$, the formal statement bounds the sum of its order-$m$ spatial derivative suprema by $C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|g_0\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and gives $\|g_0^\natural(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^{m+1}\gamma(t)\|g_0\|_{[m+1],\gamma}$, including membership in $C^{m,1/2}$. This spatial norm sums the supremum and one-half Hölder seminorm of the full multilinear derivatives through order $m$, using their operator norms.

The same bounds hold on $[0,T]$ with the unweighted norm and $\gamma$ replaced by one. If $g_0$ is independent of phase everywhere, the factor $\lambda^{3/2}$ per derivative disappears. The formal spatial derivative sum in the conclusion ranges over all ordered coordinate sequences of length $m$; the paper's sum ranges over multi-indices. Their multiplicities are bounded in terms of $m$ and absorbed into $C_m$. This physical derivative sum is distinct from the finite profile norm on the right, which counts each multi-index once.

The numbered formal statement starts with a profile defined for all labels and phases, smooth on $[0,T]$, and satisfying the coupled translation law. The paper starts with cell data whose phase average extends smoothly and periodically across the faces. Thus the numbered formal statement does not itself construct a global profile from those cell data. A separate statement constructs smooth periodic physical evaluation at a fixed time under an explicit collar condition: the profile agrees there with a smooth periodic mean. The paper's compact support in the interior of the label cell furnishes this collar; it is not a new substantive restriction. That separate statement does not assert joint smoothness in time in this form. The estimates agree once the cell data have been extended. The formal statement also allows arbitrary real normed target spaces, asserts the Hölder regularity explicitly, and uses the broader parent and seed hypotheses above. The envelope exponent is fixed first, followed by $C$ and the sequence $C_m$, before the parent and target space. The integer $C$ is independent of derivative order and no expansion depth enters this estimate.

The verdict different records both directions of change. The arbitrary target space, ordered derivative sum, and larger parent and seed classes broaden the estimates. The numbered formal statement takes the resulting smooth continuation as input, while the paper also derives it from the support and phase-mean hypotheses. The powers of $\mathsf D$ and $\lambda$, the loss of one derivative for the Hölder estimate, and the distinction between the active weighted and full unweighted intervals agree.

why: Removes an extra hypothesis and states both the abstract continuity theorem and its endpoint application.
text: Let $X$ be a real Banach space and let $S(t):X\to X$ be bounded linear isomorphisms for every real $t$. If their forward operators vary continuously in operator norm on a prescribed set $I$, then their inverses vary continuously in operator norm on $I$. No common bound on the inverse norms is a hypothesis of this statement. In Appendix A.2, take $I=[0,1]$ and $S(t)v=\mathbb P(K(t)v)$ on divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$ fields. The fixed-time inverse must first be constructed, and continuity of the forward family must be established; the theorem then supplies continuity of the inverse family.

why: Writes down the real kernel, its norm bound, and the exact evenness and completeness conditions for the usual multiplier interpretation.
text: Let $g$ be an almost-everywhere strongly measurable, essentially bounded field on the unit-volume torus $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, with values in a real normed space. Let $\Lambda>0$ and let $\psi$ be smooth and zero outside radius two. Define $H_\Lambda(z)=\sum_{|k|\le2\Lambda}\psi(k/\Lambda)e^{2\pi i k\cdot z}$ and $S^\mathbb R_\Lambda g(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^3}\operatorname{Re}H_\Lambda(x-z)g(z)\,dz$. The formal statement proves $\|S^\mathbb R_\Lambda g\|_{L^\infty}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$. For an even symbol and a Banach target, this is the paper's multiplier. Without evenness, taking the real part symmetrizes the symbol. Completeness is not assumed in the formal estimate; its integral convention assigns zero for incomplete targets. The ordinary Banach-valued integral interpretation therefore uses a complete target. This construction uses the scalar spectral kernel, not a complexification of the target. No Hölder estimate is included.

why: Displays the weighted estimates and identifies the normalized derivative families required by their hypotheses.
text: Fix a time set $I$, positive scales $\ell_*,h$ and $\gamma:I\to(0,\infty)$. For fields smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\|f\|_{[n]}$ sums $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup_{t,a,s}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^jf|$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$, once per multi-index. Assume the derivative families entering each right side below are bounded. The formal statement proves $\sum_i\|\partial_{a_i}f\|_{[n],\gamma}\le3\ell_*^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, $\|\partial_sf\|_{[n],\gamma}\le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, and $\|B(f,g)\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\|B\|\|f\|_{[n]}\|g\|_{[n],\gamma}$ for every continuous bilinear $B$. Weighted boundedness concerns derivatives of $f/\gamma$ or $g/\gamma$, not merely the unnormalized fields. For period-one Banach-valued fields, averaging, subtraction of the average and the zero-mean periodic primitive have respective bounds $1,2,2$ in the same norm; the primitive requires zero phase mean. All output derivative families are bounded. For phase-independent fields, the product estimate also holds with half-Hölder norms using the maximum of the uniform norm and seminorm. There is no time differentiation.

why: Separates the requested existence condition, terminal conclusions and the stage-limit identification used by its proof.
text: The condition asks for one integer $b$, nondecreasing threshold $\mathcal B$ and lower bound $N_1$. For every $N\ge N_1$, it requires stages with $\lambda_0=N$, eventual velocity-residual time bounds, and eventual mixed correction bounds. Their activation times tend to a positive finite $T<S_j$ for every stage. It also requires a smooth odd maximal periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$ with bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and infinite time integrals of both $\|\nabla u\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_\infty$. Both $u$ and $\partial_tu$ have every local spatial derivative limit away from $\mathbb Z^3$. The velocity extends periodically and smoothly to all real times off that lattice, with no Euler requirement after $T$. These are required properties, not their existence proof. The displayed condition shares $T$ between stages and solution but does not require $U_j\to u$; the supplied assembly proof uses that actual limit.
